images.title: Halves and thirds as sixths
images.purpose: Show the method cue for every sum: make the units the same, here sixths, then add the tops, using 1/2 + 1/3 as the warm up.
images.composition: One long number line across the middle with wide margins, two hop arcs above it, and one cue line centred below.
images.exact_structure: One straight horizontal number line from 0 to 1 in grey #6B7280 with 7 evenly spaced tick marks, 6 equal gaps of 1/6; taller ticks at 0 and 1. One wide teal #0072B2 arc above the line from 0 to the 4th tick, covering 3 gaps. One amber #E69F00 arc from the 4th tick to the 6th tick, covering 2 gaps. One reddish purple #CC79A7 ring on the 6th tick. Centred below: one cue line. Exactly 1 line, 7 ticks, 2 arcs, 1 ring.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the thirteen question sums or their results shown anywhere
images.takeaway: Make the units the same, then add the numerators.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 1 in sixths: a teal hop of 3 sixths for 1/2 and an amber hop of 2 sixths for 1/3 land on 5/6.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which common unit they will pick for each sum before starting, as in the sixths here.

image_decisions.why: The warm up sum on a number line gives the method cue without working any of the thirteen sums.
